title: Leaving The Nest
paragraphs: Oh? The ones in the nest are rather quiet. It seems that the rival’s subordinates—or rather, his kin—have grasped the situation to some extent, given the battle earlier. They stand beside the rival, letting out cries. Hearing this, the assistant looks at the rival with teary eyes.
“Anyway, Windia. I spoke today with those who are willing to take you in.”
“No… Why? I want to stay with you and everyone else!”
“Windia, please understand. You cannot find happiness here…”
“I can!”
“…There are domains for monsters, and domains for humans. I trust these people, which is why I have decided to entrust you to them. Please, listen to me. Now, come forth, heroes.”
The rival looks in our direction, calling for us.
Is this where we’re supposed to step in?
“This is really hard to walk into… but I’ll go as our representative,”

Father raises his hand with a troubled expression. Ren and Itsuki both nod. Yeah, this kind of thing should definitely be left to him. I’d rather die than deal with it myself. Father slowly approaches the rival. The assistant glares at him with intense hostility. She’s making it very clear that she has no intention of warming up to him.
“Um… I guess I’m here to take you in?”
“Yes. I leave her in your care.”
At the same time, it looks like the rival whispers something to Father.
“No! I absolutely won’t go!”
“Stop being stubborn, Windia! Now, hurry up and take her away!”
Following the rival’s orders, one of his subordinates grabs the assistant by the collar and forcibly drags her toward us.
“NOOOO! FAAAATHER!”
She reaches out toward the rival, her voice breaking into sobs. It’s a truly heart-wrenching cry. Ah, the egg she was holding rolls away. Father quickly catches it.
“Hm. I appreciate it. I leave Windia in your care.”
“Uh—ah… okay, got it.”
“FAAAATHER! NO! I WON’T GO! LET ME GO!”
The assistant is struggling desperately.
“In the end, did we just trample over a girl’s happiness?”
“Who knows?”
“Well, Ren isn’t the one killing that dragon, so maybe there’s no problem.”
“I don’t think so. That dragon wanted to return her to human society. That’s why he entrusted her to us. As painful as it is for her as his child… I think he’s a good parent.”
Ren and the others seem to be having a difficult conversation.
“Windia! Return to the human world! You are forbidden from ever coming back here! GYAAOOOOOOO!”
The rival releases a bloodthirsty aura, roaring as he glares at the assistant.
“Hii!?”
Has she never been yelled at by him before? The assistant trembles in fear. But soon, she begins to cry again.
“If you return, I will no longer consider you my child! Be prepared to face death!”
“Let me goooo! Father!”
“This is… really tough to watch…”

Father scratches his cheek, clearly at a loss. After handing the egg back to the rival, he turns and walks toward us, the assistant in tow. Then, securing his hold on her, he forcefully carries her away from the nest.
“NOOOOOO! LET ME GOOOOOO!”

The assistant struggles with all her might. We follow closely behind Father. And so, we descend the mountain. Even as we make our way down, the assistant continues to fight against Father’s grip. But by the time we reach the base, she seems to have given up, reduced to quiet sobs. All we can do is watch her with concern.
“In the end, we had to take her by force.”
“It couldn’t be helped. That dragon truly believes this is what’s best for her.”
“Hic… snff…”
“For now… um, nice to meet you. Also… I’m sorry for everything.”
The assistant completely ignores Father’s words. She continues crying as if she has shut herself away from the world.
Eventually… exhausted from sobbing, she falls into a quiet sleep. Éclair gently drapes a blanket over her and strokes her hair.
“Independence, huh…? She’s still so young, and we’ve forced her through such a painful experience.”
“Yeah… but it seems like that dragon wanted us to take care of her.”
Yuki and the others are deeply worried about the assistant. Though they despise the rival, they don’t hold the same feelings toward her.
“So? What’s the plan now?”
“Well, we’re going to meet that dragon again. He said he’d come partway with us, at least.”
“I see. But what about the girl?”
“Hmm… Éclair, Sakura, could I ask you two to watch over her?”
“Understood. Go while she’s still asleep.”
“Sakura will watch her too!”
“Yuki will keep an eye on her as well.”
Éclair, Sakura, and the others agreed to watch over the assistant.
“Alright, let’s go.”
“Yeah.”

We set off again, heading up the mountain to meet the rival once more. Not long after entering the mountain, we found him waiting for us. There was a cart with treasure piled on top of it. His subordinates had also gathered. They were within visible range if we looked carefully.
“If you’re that worried, you don’t have to leave her with us, you know… You could just come along with us instead.”
“No.”
“Sigh… Alright, then? What are you planning to do?”
“Hmm… Here is the egg that was entrusted to Windia.”
As the rival spoke, he revealed the very egg that the assistant had been carrying earlier.
“This egg, in a way, would be Windia’s younger brother or sister.”
“Yeah.”
“If the future you spoke of is true, then the one who inherited my will must be this one. And so…”

The rival spread his wings and placed a hand on the egg. Tiny lights, like fireflies, gathered around him. The egg began to glow as well. A magic circle gradually formed on the ground. It slowly shrank, its symbols engraving themselves onto the egg. Finally, the rival let a drop of his blood fall onto it.
“I have imbued this egg with a fragment of my power as Dragon Emperor… So that it will one day reach the future you spoke of.”
“Hmm… So then, what exactly is your current state?”
Father asked. That’s a fair question. He made it sound like the ‘fragment’ was his true self.
“I am only being sustained by the fragment I received from you all, just enough to have this conversation.”
The rival emitted a faint glow. His form wavered slightly.
“I thought you could function even without a core stone?”
“In that state, I would not be able to understand human speech. Some level of contingency is necessary.”
“Contingency?”
“I know that I cannot defeat you. However, if you were lying, I have prepared a means to escape with Windia.”
So, in other words…
He has placed himself inside this egg! That’s quite the trick.
“You had best be prepared to face the wrath of the Dragon Emperor at full power.”
“I’m not lying. So, I guess this is a ‘let’s work together from now on’ sort of thing?”
“…Yes. However, do not forget that the will of the one who will be born is separate from my own.”
“Sigh…”
Father responded with a troubled expression. This is such a complicated relationship. The rival turned his gaze to his subordinates. He placed a hand on the forehead of the largest one among them.
“I leave the management of my territory to you. Govern it well.”
The subordinate gave a firm nod before returning to the mountain with the others.
